subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw define execution anti-drift as a core durable run-state contract, and which artifacts, phases, blocker fields, escalation timers, feature flag, and post-green semantics should that contract enforce?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested fix selects public runtime semantics, persistence ownership, operator-visible escalation behavior, and config/flag shape across core agent execution.

options.title: Design Core Contract First
options.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

options.title: Extend Existing Primitives Only
options.body: Implement missing guarantees by extending Task Flow, heartbeat response, loop detection, lifecycle, and cron watchdog paths without creating a parallel state source.

options.title: Narrow To Reproducible Gap
options.body: Require a live transcript or replayable current-main scenario, then split only the smallest remaining status-loop or post-green idle failure into a focused issue.

recommendation.title: Design Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current routing signal across diagnostic/liveness state and recent current-main ownership among the inspected owners.
